tier2: rating >= 4 and no build red flag (weak-archetype flag excluded, see archetype_flag)

review.verdict: Removal is excellent: 4 Scorching Dragonfire, Overlord, Glassworks and Trial of Agony on a fast red curve, held back only by 13 creatures, some filler 1-drops and a thin white splash-like half.

A deep removal suite (3 Dragonfire, Nowhere to Run, Live or Die, Final Vengeance, Waltz) and Overlord on a low curve with real sac payoffs; the small, flimsy creatures like Percussionist, Glimmerlight and Playmate keep it from being exceptional.

decks.playmat_name: ★★ good_02 · WR aggro (power 2 or less) · review 4/5

review.verdict: A tight, low-curve RW aggro deck that fits its plan well. Arabella, Vicious Clowns, Midnight Mayhem and the Escorts support the small-creature theme, and Dragonfire, Glassworks, Trapped in the Screen and Sheltered by Ghosts give it solid removal. Weaker slots like Percussionist, Ragged Playmate and Shardmage's Rescue cap its ceiling.

decks.playmat_name: ★★ good_03 · BG delirium/manifest dread midrange · review 4/5

review.verdict: Solid BG midrange with strong rares (Slasher, Onslaught), double Swarmweaver, good removal and plenty of manifest bodies; only the Rats and Say Its Name are weak.

A deep removal suite with Murder, Withering Torment, Trapped in the Screen, Sheltered by Ghosts, Seized from Slumber and Nowhere to Run, plus bombs in Shroudstomper and Vile Mutilator, makes this a strong WB deck even though the creature base is thin and low-powered (Goats, Rat, Fear of Lost Teeth).

Solid BG delirium midrange with plenty of removal (Murder, 2x Live or Die, Drag to the Roots, 2x Monstrous Emergence, Bear Trap) and sturdy bodies. Card types are a bit thin for delirium, but the deck doesn't depend on it, and the curve and mana are clean.

A well-built BG delirium deck: Swarmweaver, Miasma Demon and two Fear of the Dark lead it, and the removal is strong (2 Murder, 2 Monstrous Emergence, Winter's Intervention). It has enough card types to turn on delirium reliably and a smooth curve backed by Centipede fixing. Its weak points are slightly thin black sources for the BB cards and few ways to stop fliers.

Two Overlords of the Mistmoors, three Glassworks and Trapped in the Screen give this mostly-white deck strong top end and removal. It has a solid 2-drop curve, though a few weak red cards (Turn Inside Out, Untimely Malfunction) pad out a light red half.

A low-curve, aggressive GW survivors deck with solid removal (Trapped in the Screen, Seized from Slumber, Exorcise, Monstrous Emergence), strong threats in Rip and two Fear of Exposure, and Overlord of the Mistmoors as a bomb top end; a few filler slots like Insidious Fungus, Glimmerlight and Break Down the Door keep it from being exceptional.

A solid BG delirium deck with real removal (Murder, Withering Torment, Sporogenic Infection, Monstrous Emergence) and strong top end in Overlord of the Balemurk, Swarmweaver and Miasma Demon. It is a bit light on creatures, though the manifest dread cards make up some of the gap, and Valgavoth's Faithful and Horrid Vigor are filler.

Well-built WU enchantment deck with strong synergy pieces (Enduring Innocence, Gremlin Tamers, Inquisitive Glimmer), excellent removal suite (2 Trapped in the Screen, Seized, Vanish, Floodpits, Meat Locker), and a solid 2-drop curve; token makers offset the modest creature count, though bodies are small and Duskmourn's Domination is clunky.

A real WU eerie deck: three Fear of Falling top the curve, about ten enchantments feed Tamer, Tracker and Scavenger, and Seized, Meat Locker and Vanish cover removal. Skullcrab and Shardmage's Rescue are weak filler.

A strong red-heavy Rakdos deck with plenty of removal (Chainsaw, Dragonfire, Glassworks, Winter's Intervention) and payoffs like Enduring Courage and Skinripper; three Fear of Burning Alive is a lot of 6-drops above a low curve of thin 1/1s, but the reach and removal carry it.

A coherent WU Glimmer/enchantment deck with six good removal spells (Trapped in the Screen x2, Unable to Scream x2, Seized from Slumber, Fear of Immobility), a real engine in Enduring Innocence and Lionheart Glimmer, and a low curve that suits 16 lands; its weak spots are the many 2-power bodies and little evasion, so it can stall against bigger boards.

A low-curve Rakdos deck with plenty of removal (Chainsaw, 2 Nowhere to Run, 2 Glassworks, Impossible Inferno) and good sacrifice payoffs like 2 Sawblade Skinripper and Popular Egotist; it is a bit light on cheap fodder and late-game power, but 16 lands suits the curve and it should be a strong, focused deck.

Well-built UR rooms deck: strong removal (two Dragonfire, Glassworks, Meat Locker, Drowner, Unable to Scream) and two Enduring rares on a low curve. Rooms fit the Apparition, Soulrager and Lounge payoffs, and 16 lands suit the curve. Creeping Peeper and Piggy Bank are weak filler, and the deck has little late-game power beyond the Rooms' back halves and the Megalodon.

Strong removal suite (2 Dragonfire, Bargain, Drowner, Meat Locker, Stay Hidden, Unable to Scream) plus Keybearers and Megalodons. The creature count is light and the 3-drop slot is thin, but the deck has good quality and a clear rooms plan.

A focused WG survivors deck with strong gold cards, two Fear of Abduction, Sheltered by Ghosts and Fear of Immobility for interaction, and a low curve that triggers survival well; the green is light enough that 10 Plains/7 Forest would serve the double-white cards better.

Solid GW survivors deck with a strong two-drop base and premium white removal (Hovership, Trapped in the Screen, Sheltered by Ghosts, Seized from Slumber) plus Overlord as a bomb-level top end; Overgrown Zealot is filler with no face-down synergy, but the curve and plan are sound.

A well-built UB eerie deck. Plenty of cheap removal and auras feed Skullsnap Nuisance and the recurring Fear of Infinity, and Slasher plus Fear of Falling give it real threats. Thin creature count, an empty four-drop slot and two clunky Defiled Crypts are the only soft spots.

Solid UB enchantment deck. Kaito and Miasma Demon give it a strong top end, and it has plenty of interaction: Murder, Nowhere to Run, Unable to Scream, Vanish, and two Meat Lockers. About nine enchantments keep the eerie cards working, though Piranha Flies and Fanatic are thin filler.

Deep, efficient removal (Murder, Live or Die, Drowner, Unable to Scream, two Winter's Intervention) with two Entity Trackers and enough enchantments for card advantage, topped by two strong Demons. The body count is a bit thin and the early creatures are low-impact, but this is a solid, well-built UB deck.

A tight, low-curve WU eerie deck with real payoffs: two Enduring Curiosity, Enduring Innocence and the Gremlin Tamers, plus Rooms that serve as both triggers and late-game mana sinks. The bodies are small and the hard removal is thin, but the tempo tools and card advantage should carry it.

A solid BG delirium deck. The surveil enablers and spread of card types (artifact, enchantment, instant, sorcery creatures) power up Drag to the Roots, Swarmweaver and the Cultists, and it backs that with about six real removal spells and a reasonable curve. A couple of Found Footage and Innocuous Rat are slightly low-impact.

A clean, low-curve GW survival deck with good two- and three-drops, solid removal (Trapped in the Screen, Seized from Slumber, Clobbering, Fear of Abduction) and payoffs like Tyvar and Hardened Escort, though it runs a bit thin on reach and late-game power.

A low-curve BR sacrifice deck with plenty of removal: Murder, two Betrayer's Bargain, Glassworks and Final Vengeance. Two Razorkin Hordecallers and Skinripper give it real punch; a few filler cards like Percussionist and Glimmerlight keep it from being exceptional.
Four Sawblade Skinripper, two Murder and Threaten-into-sac effects give a strong, low-curve BR sacrifice deck; Cursed Recording, two Norins and thin fodder hold it back slightly.

A focused, very low-curve RG aggro deck with a good 16-land count and payoffs like Screaming Nemesis and Vicious Clown, but several weak cards (3x Percussionist, Turn Inside Out, Norin), thin removal, and no reach mean it folds if the early rush stalls.

A solid RG beatdown core of three Fear of Being Hunted, Hordecaller, Kona, Onslaught, Dragonfire and Beatdown, with enough manifest-dread bodies to cover 13 creatures; it's diluted by half-built delirium pieces like Patchwork Beastie, 2x Say Its Name and Peer Past the Veil, so it lands as a fine but unremarkable deck.

Solid RG beatdown with a good two-drop base (3 Wickerfolk), Hordecallers and two Dragonfires, but only three real removal spells and filler like triple Cartographer and two Frantic Strength keep it from being more than a fine deck.

A low-curve, mostly-red aggro deck with a playable threaten/sacrifice subtheme and good mana, but too many weak tricks (3 Turn Inside Out, 2 Vengeful Possession) and only Betrayer's Bargain as real removal keep it merely fine.

Low-curve BR aggro deck with strong removal (Murder, Withering Torment, Betrayer's Bargain, Trial of Agony) and good threats like Razorkin Hordecaller and Fear of the Dark. It only has 14 creatures, and filler tricks like Violent Urge, Turn Inside Out and Give In to Violence make it play solid but unspectacular.

A functional BR sacrifice-aggro shell. Four Disturbing Mirth, cheap hasty fodder and solid red removal (two Glassworks, Trial of Agony, Waltz of Rage) give it a real plan. It is held back by only 13 creatures, two clunky Defiled Crypts and few strong threats.

A solid RW aggro shell with Overlord, two Midnight Mayhem, Arabella and decent removal, but it runs only 13 real creatures, has a thin three-drop slot, and plays filler like Turn Inside Out and Hand That Feeds, whose delirium never turns on here, so it is fine rather than strong.

Solid blue rooms shell with good interaction (Dragonfire, Glassworks, Meat Lockers, Fear of Falling) and Eerie payoffs, but the 13-creature count and a light, somewhat random red splash keep it a fine rather than strong deck.

A solid BR sacrifice shell: good removal (Murder, Glassworks, two Bargains), real sac fodder (Rat, Lost Teeth, Percussionist) and payoffs (Egotist, Mirth, Slasher, Fear of Burning Alive), but only 14 creatures and filler like Cracked Skull, Turn Inside Out and Ragged Playmate keep it from being great.

A playable RG beatdown deck with good threats like Hordecaller, Wickerfolk, FOMO and Slayers, but only about two real removal spells, plus filler (2x Turn Inside Out, 2x Moldering Gym, a lone Say Its Name, Norin) that dilutes the aggressive plan.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_37 · WB graveyard value midrange · review 3/5

review.verdict: A playable grindy WB deck with good removal (2 Murder, Live or Die, Hovership) and solid Glimmer Seekers, but 13 creatures feeds too little to 2 Emerge from the Cocoon and 2 Defiled Crypt, so it plays slow and clunky.

Solid UR rooms/tempo shell with good removal (2 Glassworks, Inferno, Drowners) and Enduring Curiosity, but only 13 creatures, several filler bodies, and a light rooms payoff package keep it merely fine.

A low-curve WR aggro deck on a sensible 16 lands. Arabella, double Patched Plaything, two Scorching Dragonfire, Sheltered by Ghosts and Hovership are a solid core. It loses value to cheap filler (Turn Inside Out x2, Jump Scare, Shardmage's Rescue, Norin, a Hand That Feeds that rarely gets delirium) and a thin, slow top end. Split Up is awkward to fire in an attacking deck.

A solid RG aggro shell with good removal (Betrayer's Bargain, Glassworks, Beastie Beatdown, Trial of Agony) and three Wildfire Wickerfolk, but only 13 real creatures, a thin three-drop slot, filler like Turn Inside Out, Horrid Vigor and double Glimmerlight, and few delirium enablers make it fine rather than strong.

A playable UB enchantment deck: Enduring Curiosity, Miasma Demon, two Meat Lockers and the Final Vengeances give it real power, but filler like two Valgavoth's Faithful and Fear of Lost Teeth plus small, low-impact creatures keep it a middling build.

A low-curve WR aggro deck with good pieces like Screaming Nemesis, Midnight Mayhem and Fear of Immobility, but it leans on filler: four Ragged Playmates, Hand That Feeds with delirium it can rarely turn on, and many cheap tricks in place of real removal. It's playable and will punish slow starts, but it struggles to break through stalled boards.

A low-curve WR aggro deck with good pieces like 2x Arabella, 3x Friendly Ghost and Trapped in the Screen, but four Turn Inside Out and only three real removal spells make it fragile; with this curve it could also run 16 lands.

Solid WU enchantment shell with good removal (Trapped in the Screen, Unable to Scream x2, Seized, Floodpits Drowner) and a nice top end in Wandering Rescuer, but the threats are small and the two counterspells are a weak fit for a tempo deck.

A playable BG delirium deck with solid removal (2 Murder, 2 Monstrous Emergence, Vile Mutilator) and plenty of manifest dread to fill in for the low creature count, but Walk-In Closet, double Break Down the Door and Threats Around Every Corner dilute its power.

A functional WU eerie deck with solid removal (Fear of Abduction, Trapped in the Screen, 2 Unable to Scream, Stay Hidden, Floodpits Drowner) and good enablers in Glimmers and Gremlin Tamer, but filler like Ethereal Armor, Shardmage's Rescue and Underwater Tunnel limits its power. Expect a fine, roughly average build.

A coherent WU eerie shell with a smooth, low curve and good synergy from the Entryways, Glimmers and eerie payoffs. Removal is thin (Exorcise, Fear of Abduction, the Immobility tap), and Abhorrent Oculus is nearly uncastable with no self-mill. Playable, but it lacks power.

A coherent RW small-creature aggro deck with real payoffs (Arabella, 2x Midnight Mayhem, Vicious Clown, Irreverent Gremlin). Light removal (Chainsaw, Glassworks) and filler like 3x Clockwork Percussionist and 2x Turn Inside Out keep it from being more than fine, and the low curve could run 16 lands.

A deep removal suite, led by four Seized from Slumber, Trapped in the Screen and Fear of Abduction, plus Twins value make this a solid grindy deck, but the finishers are thin and the Faithful/Fanatic filler is low-impact.

A coherent UG manifest deck with good blue tempo cards (Drowner, Vanish from Sight, Meat Locker, Fear of Isolation) and plenty of face-down bodies, but filler like 3 Spineseeker, Don't Make a Sound and Threats, plus little real removal, makes it solid but unspectacular.

A playable, cohesive BG deck with good pieces in The Swarmweaver, Unstoppable Slasher, Fear of Exposure, and the cycling top end. Removal is thin and mostly creature-dependent (Clobbering, Monstrous Emergence), and filler like Valgavoth's Faithful, Give In to Violence and Patchwork Beastie holds it to an average build.

Strong red removal suite (Dragonfire, Bargain, 2x Glassworks, Inferno, Beatdown) and solid aggressive threats, but only 13 creatures and loose delirium enablers make it a decent rather than great RG deck.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_53 · WR aggro (power 2 or less) · review 3/5

review.verdict: A coherent, low-curve WR small-creatures deck with good removal (2x Trapped in the Screen, Dragonfire, Glassworks, Inferno) and Arabella as a payoff, but many bodies are low-impact 2/2s and 1/1s with little reach, so it can stall against bigger boards.

A real UG manifest shell built on 3x Growing Dread, Cryptid Inspectors, and Bookworm. But the creature count is light and the blue is thin, so it plays more like mono-green with some filler (Say Its Name, Cathartic Parting) and an awkward Altanak.

A solid black core with Overlord, two Murders, Withering Torment and Snatcher, plus a low curve. The light white splash of 2-drops and Glimmerlights is filler, so it plays fine but lacks threats that win games.

Overlord, Onslaught and the fight-style removal carry it, but the bodies are small for Clobbering and Emergence, the four black cards don't justify seven Swamps, and two 7-drop Altanaks with only two Say Its Name make the late game slow.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_57 · WG G-heavy midrange splashing W · review 3/5

review.verdict: A solid, low-curve green deck. Four Flesh Burrowers, Fear of Exposure and Wickerfolk Thresher give it real pressure, and it has decent removal. But the white is shallow, delirium is hard to turn on, and there's little late-game power, so it's fine rather than strong.

A playable WB curve deck with good white survivors (two Savior of the Small, Glimmer Seeker), solid removal in Hovership and Trapped in the Screen, and Vile Mutilator as a finisher. Light removal and filler like two Emerge from the Cocoon, Orphans and Valgavoth's Faithful keep it average.

A cohesive low-curve WU eerie deck with good removal (Trapped in the Screen, Sheltered by Ghosts, Unable to Scream, Vanish) and Gremlin Tamer synergy, but the creatures are small, it has almost no top end besides Shepherding Spirits, and some filler (Shardmage's Rescue, Get Out) keeps it a solid but unspectacular deck.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_60 · RG manifest dread midrange · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid RG manifest deck: the 2-drops are dense, there are good bite and burn effects, and Altanak, Hordecaller and the Beasties close games, but delirium payoffs are unreliable and card quality is good rather than great.
Strong removal suite (2 Murder, 2 Seized, Exorcise) and decent card advantage carry a deck whose creature base is thin and low-impact, with several slow Room enchantments diluting the threat count.

A coherent WU eerie deck: Gremlin Tamers, Inquisitive Glimmer and the Glimmer-makers synergize well and Overlord of the Floodpits is a premium top end, but with no hard removal (only Stay Hidden, Unnerving Grasp and Fear of Immobility tempo) and filler like Scrabbling Skullcrab, it's a solid but unspectacular build.

A coherent WU eerie deck with good enablers like Entity Tracker, Optimistic Scavenger, Glimmer Seeker and the token makers, plus strong fliers in two Fear of Falling and Fear of Abduction. Only 13 real creatures, several low-impact bodies like Piranha Fly and Unsettling Twins, and thin true removal make it a solid but unspectacular deck.

A coherent UG manifest shell: Shrieker, Inspector, Bookworm, Analyst and Fear of Falling give it a real plan, and the cyclers smooth the mana. Removal is thin, and filler like two Machetes, two Say Its Name and an unreliable Patchwork Beastie keeps it at a fine but unexceptional level.

Solid BG delirium shell with 3 Broodspinner, Swarmweaver, Sticktwister and good enablers. Removal is light (2 Murder, Winter's Intervention), and the two Altanaks are a clunky top end, but the curve and mana are fine.

Solid removal suite (Murder, 2 Exorcise, Nowhere to Run, Sheltered by Ghosts, Live or Die) and a good curve, but only about seven enchantments to feed the eerie payoffs. Filler like Possessed Goat, Ethereal Armor and Emerge from the Cocoon plus few strong threats keep it a fine, unspectacular deck.

A solid RG deck with plenty of removal (Chainsaw, Dragonfire, Beatdown, Clobbering, Glassworks) and a strong top end in two Hordecallers, but at 13 creatures its many fight/bite spells can strand, and filler like Patchwork Beastie and Hand That Feeds leans hard on delirium.

Solid UR midrange with plenty of removal (Dragonfire x2, Glassworks x2, Unable to Scream x2, Drowner) and a reasonable curve, but its threats are mediocre and Abhorrent Oculus is nearly uncastable with no self-mill.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_69 · RG manifest dread midrange · review 3/5

review.verdict: A solid RG manifest-dread midrange deck with a real top end (Altanak, Branchsnapper, Hordecaller, Beastie) and two Glassworks, but it is light on removal and padded with weak cards like Say Its Name, Turn Inside Out, Percussionist and Fungus; the many manifest effects help make up for only 13 true creatures.
Solid green-heavy delirium deck with strong top end in Overlord, Tyvar and Enduring Vitality, plus good early drops, but thin on interaction, and the blue splash-level cards are mostly filler.

A coherent, low-curve BR sacrifice deck: Sawblade Skinripper x2, cheap fodder (Fear of Lost Teeth, Innocuous Rat, Piggy Bank, Glimmer tokens) and sacrifice-based removal (Final Vengeance x2, Betrayer's Bargain) fit together well, but filler like Ghost Vacuum and Defiled Crypt plus little reach or late-game power keep it at a solid but unspectacular level.

A solid green-heavy midrange deck with good bodies, Altanak and Enduring Curiosity at the top end and decent manifest synergy, but almost no real removal, so it has to win by out-sizing opponents and can lose to fliers or bombs.

Plenty of real removal (Murder, Nowhere to Run, Trapped in the Screen, Seized from Slumber, two Winter's Intervention) and a strong top end in two Shroudstompers, Shepherding Spirits and Enduring Innocence. But the threat base is thin and mediocre: Goat, Faithful, Teddy and the Fanatics are filler, and the double-pip costs strain an 8/8 manabase. A solid, grindy deck rather than a great one.

Plenty of cheap removal and a real sacrifice plan with Skinripper, Ripper, Bargain and Final Vengeance, but four Percussionists and few sturdy threats make the clock thin, and 17 lands is a lot for this low curve.

A coherent UG manifest dread deck. Growing Dread, Paranormal Analyst, Bookworm and the many dread effects work together, and there is solid fight-style removal, but it is light on real creatures and leans on reactive counters and a delirium card it can't reliably turn on.

Solid BG curve with good two-drops and quality removal (Come Back Wrong, Drag to the Roots, Monstrous Emergence). Graveyard enablers are modest and the five-drop slot is empty, so it plays as a fine but unspectacular midrange deck that relies on Spectral Snatchers and Onslaught to close.

A solid, low-curve UG deck with good removal (Unable to Scream, Clobbering, Emergence, Drowner) and Valgavoth's Onslaught as a mana sink, but it is thin on power past four mana and the delirium payoffs are unreliable.

A playable WG deck with real removal (Hovership, Seized from Slumber, Clobbering, Exorcise) and good survivors like Glimmer Seeker and Savior of the Small, but 13 creatures, two Surgical Suites, and a thin threat base hold it to average.

A low-curve UR tempo deck with good top cards in Enduring Curiosity, Fear of Falling, two Glassworks, Floodpits Drowner and Boilerbilges Ripper, plus enough Glimmers and Rooms for the Entity Trackers, but Ragged Playmates, Untimely Malfunction and Piranha Fly are filler, it has few ways to pull ahead, and with this curve it could run 16 lands.

A solid, low-curve UR deck with plenty of cheap removal (2 Dragonfire, Glassworks, Meat Locker, Unable to Scream) and decent Room synergy. Its threats are mediocre and Oculus is hard to enable without self-mill, so it plays as a fine but unspectacular deck.

Solid UG shell with Oculus, Altanak, Megalodon, and good removal like Clobbering, Emergence, and Vanish, but only 13 creatures, a lone Say Its Name, and a delirium-dependent Beastie keep it a fine deck rather than a strong one.

Solid UG tempo-value deck. Fear of Falling, the Meat Lockers, Unable to Scream and Valgavoth's Onslaught give it real power, and Keybearer/Peeper reward the rooms, but the removal is soft and the creature quality is middling.

A focused, low-curve GW survival deck with three Shrewd Storytellers and solid two-drops, but it relies on Sheltered by Ghosts as its only real removal and has some filler (3 Cartographers, Horrid Vigor), so it is fine rather than strong.

A solid, cohesive WG beatdown deck: Lionheart Glimmers, Fear of Exposure, Storytellers and Baseball Bat give real pressure. Removal is thin (Trapped in the Screen, Sheltered by Ghosts, Monstrous Emergence), Patchwork Beastie rarely turns on in this shell, and three Unsettling Twins are filler.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_85 · WG G(w) manifest dread midrange · review 3/5

review.verdict: A solid, cohesive green manifest-dread deck: good 2-drops, three Bashful Beasties, Rip and plenty of extra bodies from manifests. It has only one real removal spell and almost no evasion, so it can stall against fliers or bombs.

A committed UR Rooms deck. Both Soulrager pairs, Glassworks, Betrayer's Bargain, Fear of Impostors and Enduring Curiosity give it real payoffs and interaction. Filler like two Central Elevators, Skullcrab and Peeper leaves it short on pressure and card quality, so it's playable but middling.

A low-curve UB flier deck with real power in Kaito, Fear of Falling, Floodpits Drowner, Fear of Impostors and Vile Mutilator, plus solid cheap removal. Two Don't Make a Sound, Creeping Peeper and Cracked Skull are weak filler, and the deck has little card advantage, so it plays as a fine but not exceptional tempo deck.

A solid GW body-and-removal deck: Trapped in the Screen, Sheltered by Ghosts, Exorcise, Onslaught, Dissection Tools and Wurm/Altanak give it real power, but Cathartic Parting, Insidious Fungus, Overgrown Zealot and an often-stranded Patchwork Beastie hold it back from being better than fine.

A solid UR aggro-tempo deck built around two Enduring Curiosity, Fear of Burning Alive and real Room/enchantment synergy with Entity Tracker and Unwilling Vessel. It has a good 2-3 drop curve and clean mana, but only Dragonfire and Inferno count as true removal, and the Glimmerlights and Ticket Booths are mediocre filler.

A real eerie plan with 4 Balemurk Leech, Entity Tracker and Fear of Infinity backed by rooms and enchantment creatures, plus a low curve. Removal is thin (Withering Torment, Meat Locker, Cracked Skull) and filler like Ghost Vacuum, Piranha Fly and Valgavoth's Faithful makes it a fine but unspectacular deck.

Solid UB shell with real power in Enduring Tenacity, Fear of the Dark, Live or Die, Duskmourn's Domination, Meat Locker and Spectral Snatcher. It is held back by a light 13-creature count and low-impact filler like Innocuous Rat, Creeping Peeper and Paranormal Analyst. The Mindskinner also turns the rest of the team's damage into mill instead of a clean clock.

A coherent UB eerie shell with good enablers like Entity Tracker, Skullsnap Nuisance and recurring Fears of Infinity, plus solid top-end in Miasma Demon and Fear of the Dark. Hard removal is thin and filler like Enter the Enigma, Cracked Skull and Fanatic drags it down to a fine, not great, deck.

A focused Rooms deck with good removal: 2 Dragonfire, Glassworks, Meat Locker and 3 Furnace, plus Curiosity and Keybearer as payoffs. The creature base is thin and has weak filler like Skullcrab, Enter the Enigma and Playmate, so it is a solid deck but not a great one.

Nearly mono-blue, cohesive Rooms/eerie deck with good blue commons (Fear of Falling x2, Unable to Scream x2, Drowner, Fear of Impostors), but little real removal, a weak Central Elevator slot and a thin black splash keep it a solid but unexceptional deck.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_95 · RG+b midrange splash B · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid red removal suite (Dragonfire, 2x Glassworks, Inferno, Beatdown) on a reasonable RG midrange body. Light on creatures, with the manifest dread cards counted. 2x Say Its Name without Altanak and the one-card Swarmweaver splash are mediocre choices, so this is a fine deck rather than a strong one.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_96 · UG+w manifest/eerie with W splash · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid UG core in Growing Dread, Entity Tracker, Meat Locker x2, Onslaught and Beasties, but removal is thin, it has only 13 creatures, and the splash for one mediocre Toby is wasted. Oculus is hard to enable without self-mill, and Mindskinner works against the rest of the deck's damage.

Solid WB value deck with good removal (Murder, Hovership, Sheltered, 2x Live or Die, Nowhere to Run, Mutilator) and strong top end (Shroudstomper), but only 13 creatures and a clunky 4-5 slot keep it from being great.

Solid removal (Murder, Seized from Slumber, Trapped in the Screen, Miasma Demon) and strong top end in Shroudstomper and Spectral Snatcher, but only 13 creatures, filler bodies like 3x Fanatic of the Harrowing, too many reanimation spells, and 8 Plains for a heavily black, BB-costed deck make it a fine but clunky build.

A solid UB eerie shell with plenty of removal. About 12 enchantments recur Fear of Infinity and power Final Vengeance, and Enduring Curiosity plus Miasma Demon give it a strong top end. It is held back by thin, low-power threats: three Fear of Failed Tests, two Fanatics and Killer's Mask, with only 13 real creatures.
